name: Print
description: Prints a message: printf with the format in argument 0 and its values after it (debug messages such as "POS POS_RYOU_0 = %f, %f, %f.")

name: StartThread
description: Starts a thread of the program: the function in argument 0, the number of its arguments in argument 1, and those arguments. Returns the thread

name: KillThread
description: Ends the thread in argument 0 (0: the current one). Returns 1 if it was running

name: DebugText
description: Draws a debug text when a debug flag of the game is set: argument 0 and 1 the position (column and row), argument 2 a printf format (e.g. "Volume = %3d") and its values after it

name: FloatMath
description: Operation on floats chosen by argument 0 (comparisons, conversions, differences of vectors), on the next arguments

name: MapCamera
description: Shows the camera of the ECAM chunk of the map whose ID is argument 0 (e.g. 2019 for the camera "2019"), through the camera controller of the game (mode 3). Arguments 1 and 2 are the IDs of two characters, or 0: the relative cameras (flag 0x200) are shown with a character (e.g. 'AKIR', 'TBOX')

name: SetPosition
description: Sets the position of the character of ID argument 0 (the word 0x08 of the character, as Position of the CHRT scripts) from the vector of 3 floats at argument 2. Argument 1 has flags: 0x20000000, 0x10000000 and 0x08000000 select X, Y and Z (0x38000000: the three), 0x80000000 adds the vector to the position instead, and 0x40000000 uses another space (the word 0x04 and the functions around it)

name: GetPosition
description: Copies the position of the character of ID argument 0 to the vector at argument 2: its own position (argument 1: -1) or that of its node of argument 1. Argument 3 has flags, 0x40000000 as for SetPosition (0x018)

name: GetAngle
description: Copies the angles of the character of ID argument 0 (the words 0x14 to 0x1C, as Angle of the CHRT scripts) to the vector at argument 1, each one masked with 0xFFFF. Argument 2 has flags, 0x40000000 as for SetPosition (0x018)

name: SetAngle
description: Sets the angles of the character of ID argument 0 from the vector at argument 2, with the flags of SetPosition (0x018) in argument 1 (0x38000000: X, Y and Z, 0x10000000: only Y, the direction it faces). Argument 3 is passed to the function that turns it. Returns a value

name: TurnTowards
description: Computes the direction from the position of the character of ID argument 0 to the point at argument 2 (with the arctangent function at 0x0C0915E0) and sets it as with SetAngle (0x01D), with its flags (argument 1) and argument 3

name: CharacterDisplay
description: The display flag of the character of ID argument 0, the one that the flag DISP of the CHRT scripts sets (flag 3 of the byte of flags at 0x0C0AB3B8): argument 1 equal to 1 sets it, 2 clears it, 0 returns it

name: PlayMotion
description: Plays a motion on the character of ID argument 0, through its motion module (ID MOTM): argument 1 is the motion ID (e.g. 724), stored in the module, which clears its bit 0x02 (see MotionEnded, 0x029). Arguments 2 to 4 are floats (usually -1), argument 5 the speed (usually 1.0, the field that MotionSpeed, 0x04E, sets), argument 6 unknown

name: MotionEnded
description: Returns the bit 0x02 of the motion module of the character of ID argument 0, cleared by PlayMotion (0x028): the programs wait for it after playing a motion (while it returns 0)

name: Fade
description: Probably a fade of the screen: a duration in argument 0 and two colors (red, green, blue, alpha) in the next 8 arguments. With -1, returns its state

name: CharacterKill
description: Calls on the character of ID argument 0 the function of the flag KILL of the CHRT scripts (0x0C0AACE4), with argument 1 (always 1)

name: MotionSpeed
description: *Probably* the speed of the motions of the character of ID argument 0: sets the float of argument 1 (1.0, 1.3...) in the field of its motion module that PlayMotion (0x028) sets from its argument 5, and in another one 0x38 bytes after it

name: Cutscene
description: Cutscenes of the table of 70 slots of the map (the TRCK chunk n of the SCEX chunk is the cutscene n; game_13E loads others): with argument 0 from 0 to 69, plays the cutscene of that slot. Negative values are other operations: -1 returns the state of the cutscene being played (the programs wait while it is not 0), -8 returns a flag of the slot of argument 1 and -12 sets it to argument 2, -4 and -5 set and clear a flag of the cutscene being played, -6 stops it

name: GameFlags
description: Flags and values of the game, the operation in argument 0: 11 returns the flag of argument 1 (0 to 1023, bits of the 128 bytes at 0x0C225AE8) and 12 sets it to argument 2; 13 and 14 the same with the 64 flags at 0x0C225AE0; 15 returns the byte of argument 1 (0 to 31, at 0x0C225B68) and 16 sets it. The other operations (0, 1, 2, 6 to 10, 0x11 to 0x1E) do other things. The programs use the flags 5 to 1023 and the bytes 3 to 31

name: GetDate
description: Copies the date and the hour of the game to the 7 bytes pointed by argument 0: the year minus 1900 (86 for 1986), the month, the day, the day of the week, the hour, the minute and the second

name: SoundCommand
description: *Probably* a command to the sound driver: argument 0 is a command in the style of MIDI (its high nibble selects the function, at 0x0C1D6400 to 0x0C1D67A8), arguments 1 and 2 a channel and a value (the value masked with 0x7F)

name: PlayVoice
description: Probably plays a voice clip, named in argument 0 (e.g. "SY11A006")

name: LoadMotionBank
description: Loads a motion file (MOTN, m_*.bin) named in argument 2 (e.g. "M_TPIN.BIN") from scene/NN/<folder>, NN being argument 0 and the folder the 4-character ID of argument 1 (e.g. 'FREE', 'D000'); "M_MOBJ.BIN" and "M_MDOR.BIN" are loaded from misc instead. Returns a value

name: MapModelDisplay
description: Shows (argument 1: 1) or hides (0) the MAP model of the slot of argument 0, in a table of 32 (0x0C21E328, 0x60 bytes each): slot 0 is MAP.MT5 and slot n MAPnn.MT5. Returns the previous value

name: ArrayAccess
description: Operation chosen by argument 1 (18 operations) on the element of argument 2 of the array of argument 0, of bytes, halfwords or words

name: CharacterActive
description: Wakes (argument 1: 1) or puts to sleep (0) the character of ID argument 0: the same flag (bit 0x04 of the word 0x5C of the character) that the flag SLEEP of the CHRT scripts clears, with the same calls

name: VoicePlaying
description: Returns 1 while the voice of argument 0 is playing (a value returned by PlayVoice, 0x06D), or with 0, while any of the 2 voices is: the programs wait after PlayVoice until it returns 0

name: ScrollSprite
description: *Probably* the sprites of the scrolls (SPR files of the sprite folder, e.g. sprite/scroll00.spr), the operation in argument 0: 0 loads the file of argument 2 from the folder of argument 1 ("sprite"); 1 to 5 other operations

name: VoiceArchive
description: Probably opens (argument 0: 1) or closes (0) the archive of voices named in argument 1 (e.g. "E1032", "SY11")

name: LoadHmotFile
description: Loads a HMOT_*.BIN file (argument 2, e.g. "HMOT_CAN.BIN") of the loaded package of argument 1, or else from scene/NN/<folder> (NN: argument 0, folder: the 4-character ID of argument 1, e.g. 'VEND'), and adds it to a list. Returns it

name: SoundBanks
description: Probably sets the sound banks of the 8 slots at once, a name per argument (e.g. "system1.snd", "amb022.snd", "FREE" to empty the slot, 0 to keep it), as the commands of the SNDD chunk

name: DebugMessage
description: Does nothing in this version: the programs pass it error messages (e.g. "Don't make BOX Buffer!!\n")

name: Package
description: Packages (PKF/PKS files), in a table of 32 loaded ones, the operation in arguments 0 and 1. (0, 0): starts loading the package named in argument 3 from the folder of argument 2 (e.g. "scene/01/JOMO", "COMMON01"), returning 0 if it is already loaded; (0, 2): returns the state of the loading (the programs wait while it isn't 0); (0, 5): returns 1 if the package of argument 2 is loaded; (0, 6): frees it; (0, 8): loads the PKF and PKS pair of entries argument 3 and 4 of the AFS file of argument 2 (OP99.afs). (2, 2) and (2, 3) take a package by name too

name: SequenceData
description: Cutscenes of the table of 70 slots played by game_050, the slot in argument 1: with argument 0 equal to 0, loads in it the AUTH file named in argument 2 (e.g. "seqdata1.bin": SEQDATA1.AUTH) from the package of argument 3 (e.g. "D0W0": d0w0.pks)

name: SoundBank
description: Sound banks in slots, the operation in argument 0: with 0, loads the bank of argument 2 (or "FREE") in the slot of argument 1

name: Weather
description: The weather of the game (WEATHER.BIN), the operation in argument 0: 12 returns the events of the day of the FCAS chunk for argument 1 equal to 0 (bit 1: snow on the ground, 2: Christmas, 3: New Year), their bit 0 to 3 for 2 to 5, and for 1 whether the day has no event; 11 reads the low byte of the entry of a date (arguments 1 to 3). The operations 4 to 10 take a date (arguments 1 to 5) and probably return values of the curves of the clouds, the rain and the snow

name: LoadingScreen
description: *Probably* the loading screen (its code uses LOADNUM.GZ, LSCN and the sprite folder): argument 0 equal to 1 calls one function, 0 and 2 another one with 0 or 1 and, for 2, argument 1 (a map ID such as 'MFSY')
